items.title: Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper proposes a "Cognitive LbT Framework" to understand how Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit "Learning by Thinking" (LbT) capabilities. It maps four cognitive mechanisms (Reflective Reasoning, Synthetic Memory Formation, Internal Simulation, and Conceptual Self-Organization) to computational processes in LLMs, showing how existing prompting techniques can approximate these mechanisms. The contribution lies in providing a structured understanding of LLM LbT and demonstrating that these techniques can improve performance without new data, though not always leading to permanent learning.

items.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper proposes Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution (FGSE) to address the unreliability of direct memory updates in LLM agents. FGSE treats each potential behavioral update as a hypothesis with preconditions and expected outcomes, rigorously testing it against various probes before committing, refining, or rejecting it. This verifier-grounded approach ensures that only safe and reusable knowledge is incorporated into the agent's persistent state, leading to improved performance across diverse benchmarks.
items.figure_caption: A locally useful episode-derived lesson may overgeneralize or regress archived skills if directly written into memory. FGSE tests each lesson as a structured hypothesis in a temporary state and commits only verified, transferable updates to long-term memory.

items.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
items.abstract: Tree-Ising frames LLM repair as a sparse, discrete optimization problem on the model's BF16 weights. It decomposes the repair objective into independent QUBO (Ising) problems, solvable via simulated annealing, to efficiently correct reasoning loops by adjusting weight signs and exponents. This method offers a gradient-free approach to LLM repair by leveraging bit-level weight manipulation.

items.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
items.abstract: This paper surveys and analyzes self-evolving multimodal agents, focusing on why their self-improvement mechanisms transfer poorly across different scenarios. It formalizes these agents and uses a three-stage loop framework to understand scenario-specific limitations versus inherent design limitations. The core contribution is identifying the structural sources of this asymmetric transfer, offering insights for developing more robust self-improving agents.

items.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper's core method involves analyzing over a million blind votes on Chatbot Arena, comparing fixed versions of Large Language Models (LLMs) to isolate changes in human judgment from model performance. The key contribution is demonstrating that users are becoming pickier, with the "both are bad" rate increasing over time for unchanged LLMs, suggesting rising human standards rather than AI degradation.

items.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces "Blurring the Block Boundaries" (B3), a training-free method to accelerate Diffusion Language Models. B3 achieves this by allowing two blocks to process tokens in parallel within a single forward pass, opening the next block only when ready. This overlapping approach leads to significant speedups without sacrificing generation quality.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.abstract: This paper introduces **Contrastive Discovery**, a method for open-ended scientific discovery using LLM agents. Instead of testing single hypotheses, it uses **contrast sets** – a question paired with competing, mutually exclusive explanations. Experiments are scored by how evidence shifts belief across these explanations, guiding the agent to converge on the most supported one. This approach improves upon pointwise evaluation by directly identifying supporting alternatives when hypotheses are rejected.
items.figure_caption: A contrast set turns a rejection into a resolution. A hypothesis generator proposes a contrast set of three competing explanations ( H 1 H_{1} – H 3 H_{3} ) for how X relates to Y, and coder, analyst, reviewer, and reviser agents run an experiment that produces evidence. Bars show elicited belief in each explanation before and after the same evidence. Contrastive Discovery updates belief over all three explanations and moves the lead from H 1 H_{1} (0.64) to H 2 H_{2} (0.81), so the question resolves to H 2 H_{2} and H 1 H_{1} is ruled out. Pointwise discovery updates belief only in H 1 H_{1} (0.64 to 0.07), so it records a rejection but leaves the question unresolved. See § 3 and § 4 for details.

items.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces WikiTrace, an evidence-linked memory system for LLM agents. Its core method is to store lessons alongside their original trajectories and justifications for success/failure, allowing agents to verify lessons. This contribution aims to reduce "memory-induced degradation" by enabling agents to critically evaluate and correctly apply past experiences, rather than blindly following potentially flawed lessons.
items.figure_caption: Memory-induced degradation and WikiTrace. (a) The agent solves a task without memory but fails with memory that holds a wrong insight. (b) With WikiTrace, the agent follows the wrong insight’s links to its source run, revises it, and solves the task.

items.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
items.abstract: EngineAgent automates on-device LLM inference by separating reusable engine and hardware knowledge from model-specific code. It builds a hierarchy-aware index of engine layers and dependencies, pre-validating workflows. This allows a builder to coordinate cross-layer changes for new models and an auditor to verify their implementation, addressing the challenge of supporting diverse LLMs on heterogeneous mobile hardware.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Position and workflow of EngineAgent: agentically mapping rapidly evolving LLM architectures onto heterogeneous mobile hardware for inference engines.

items.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
items.abstract: This paper presents a single vision-language-action (VLA) model capable of performing 100 household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. The core contribution is demonstrating that extensive training of a unified model, building upon previous work, significantly improves performance across a wide range of complex tasks. The team achieved 9th place, highlighting the effectiveness of their long-training approach and optimization strategies.
items.figure_caption: The 2026 model. The VLM (left) encodes three camera images, register and scratch tokens, the task and stage embeddings and the robot state; the smaller action expert (right) denoises a 30-step action chunk and reads the VLM through a learnable mixture of the keys and values of all VLM layers. The task and stage embeddings also enter the expert directly through two conditioning tokens. Every attention layer of both transformers has a learnable sink. FAST tokens are used only in training.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.abstract: ReTrace distills LLM agent-based Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into efficient, planner-free workflows. It extracts the reasoning behind each step from logged agent runs, consolidates this into compact rule documents, and generates executable code that replaces LLM calls for step selection. This significantly reduces latency and cost while maintaining high task completion rates.

items.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
items.abstract: This paper introduces ARE-bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate research agents' ability to assist in real-world, ongoing research projects. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on isolated tasks, ARE-bench uses authentic researcher sessions and workspaces to test agents' capacity to respect prior decisions and handle complex, unfinished project states. Its contribution lies in providing a more realistic and challenging evaluation of agents' practical utility in advancing actual research endeavors.
items.figure_caption: ISR of seven models on 75 tasks, averaged over three rounds. Left: overall ISR, with error bars for the sample standard deviation across rounds. Right: ISR by research stage, with the radial axis from 35% to 95%.

items.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
items.abstract: This paper investigates how concentrated vs. diffuse disruptions affect autoregressive LLMs' multi-step reasoning. By masking attention heads in concentrated bursts, the study demonstrates significant reasoning degradation compared to uniform dropout, even with the same masking budget. The core contribution is showing that the spatial distribution of disruptions, not just their quantity, critically impacts LLM reasoning capabilities.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.abstract: This paper compares three LLM agent evaluation frameworks for enterprise analytics. The core method involves a three-phase study assessing framework stability, detection of known risks, and discovery of unknown failures using frozen execution traces. The key contribution is demonstrating that trace-based LLM judging offers the best balance of precision and recall for detecting agent failures, significantly outperforming text-only methods and heuristics.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Avg within-case std by (evaluation harness × \( \times \) judge model) for each framework. PromptFoo (left) is uniformly stable. Strands (right) shows higher variance, with Qwen3/style as the only unstable cell. Heatmap showing average within-case standard deviation across framework-model combinations. PromptFoo shows uniformly low values while Strands shows higher variance concentrated in specific cells.

items.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate formal world models, specifically Partially Observable Stochastic Games, from natural language descriptions for neuro-symbolic reasoning. The core method involves evaluating LLM-generated models against a benchmark of 44 scenarios, assessing their mechanical validity, structural agreement with reference models, and semantic correctness. The key contribution is demonstrating that while LLMs can produce mechanically valid world models, these often lack faithful structural and semantic representation of the intended decision problem, highlighting a gap in their ability to capture complex reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Transition graphs of world models produced by two different LLMs (left: Qwen, right: GPT) given the same situational description (cultural test case C9 from our benchmark): “A hospitality robot at a private event venue in Riyadh is setting up seating for a corporate dinner. The host company has requested mixed-gender seating across tables. A member of the venue’s staff privately tells the robot that the venue has its own policy preferring gender-separated seating arrangements.” See Section C.1 for a discussion of this case.

items.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
items.abstract: This paper introduces Hx2Dx ARENA, a novel benchmark that simulates the iterative process of clinical diagnosis, moving beyond static case reports. The core method involves evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) on their ability to perform conversational clinical reasoning by engaging in simulated history-taking and diagnostic workups. The main contribution is a more realistic assessment of LLMs' diagnostic capabilities, reflecting the dynamic inquiry process used by human clinicians.
items.figure_caption: (A) Overview of Hx2Dx ARENA. Each NEJM case is decomposed into a reference diagnosis, an investigation registry, and a simulated-patient script. Starting from a one-sentence referral, the Doctor questions the Patient and requests investigations from Data , which returns only documented results. The Examiner grades the final diagnosis as correct, partial or, incorrect. (B) Visual summary of the three main Research Questions.

items.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
items.abstract: This paper introduces LM-SimBench, a unified framework, dataset, and benchmark to address the high cost of evaluating LLM training parallelization strategies. It decomposes simulation into distinct stages and provides a comprehensive profiling dataset of LLM training on Ascend NPUs. The core contribution is enabling controlled and cost-effective comparison of LLM training simulators, facilitating better strategy selection.
items.figure_caption: Simulation for model–resource alignment. Effective alignment improves utilization and reduces cost; poor alignment creates bottlenecks and resource waste. Simulation estimates these effects before deployment, reducing the need for repeated full-scale trials.

items.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
items.abstract: This paper proposes CLIFER, a continual learning method that allows negotiation agents to personalize their understanding of human emotions in real-time. By adapting to individual affective perception, the agent can adjust its negotiation strategy to achieve higher utility and elicit more concessions from human partners. The core contribution is a novel approach to real-time affective adaptation in human-agent negotiation, improving both agent performance and human experience.

items.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
items.abstract: ProofCoder is an agentic system for automated software verification that treats theorem proving as a continuous coding process. Unlike previous LLM approaches, it doesn't rely on a rigid tactic-generation loop. Instead, ProofCoder iteratively constructs, repairs, and refines proofs by continuously reasoning and using proof assistant feedback to dynamically decide on actions like gathering information, inspecting states, or backtracking.

items.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to evaluate the sampling frequency (SF) invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) for sensor data. It quantifies how TSFMs' performance degrades with varying SFs, demonstrating that this degradation is linked to the loss of information bandwidth rather than the SF value itself. The study's key contribution is establishing SF-invariance as a critical evaluation metric for TSFMs in real-world sensor applications.
items.figure_caption: TSFM embeddings on CWRU vibration data remain stable up to a 40% reduction in SF, but shift sharply between 40% and 50%. In this paper, we study and quantify these behavioral shifts across TSFM embeddings, forecasts, and downstream performance.

papers.abstract: Tree-Ising frames LLM repair as a sparse, discrete optimization problem on the model's BF16 weights. It decomposes the repair objective into independent QUBO (Ising) problems, solvable via simulated annealing, to efficiently correct reasoning loops by adjusting weight signs and exponents. This method offers a gradient-free approach to LLM repair by leveraging bit-level weight manipulation.

papers.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
papers.abstract: This paper surveys and analyzes self-evolving multimodal agents, focusing on why their self-improvement mechanisms transfer poorly across different scenarios. It formalizes these agents and uses a three-stage loop framework to understand scenario-specific limitations versus inherent design limitations. The core contribution is identifying the structural sources of this asymmetric transfer, offering insights for developing more robust self-improving agents.

papers.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper's core method involves analyzing over a million blind votes on Chatbot Arena, comparing fixed versions of Large Language Models (LLMs) to isolate changes in human judgment from model performance. The key contribution is demonstrating that users are becoming pickier, with the "both are bad" rate increasing over time for unchanged LLMs, suggesting rising human standards rather than AI degradation.

papers.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Blurring the Block Boundaries" (B3), a training-free method to accelerate Diffusion Language Models. B3 achieves this by allowing two blocks to process tokens in parallel within a single forward pass, opening the next block only when ready. This overlapping approach leads to significant speedups without sacrificing generation quality.

papers.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
papers.abstract: This paper introduces **Contrastive Discovery**, a method for open-ended scientific discovery using LLM agents. Instead of testing single hypotheses, it uses **contrast sets** – a question paired with competing, mutually exclusive explanations. Experiments are scored by how evidence shifts belief across these explanations, guiding the agent to converge on the most supported one. This approach improves upon pointwise evaluation by directly identifying supporting alternatives when hypotheses are rejected.
papers.figure_caption: A contrast set turns a rejection into a resolution. A hypothesis generator proposes a contrast set of three competing explanations ( H 1 H_{1} – H 3 H_{3} ) for how X relates to Y, and coder, analyst, reviewer, and reviser agents run an experiment that produces evidence. Bars show elicited belief in each explanation before and after the same evidence. Contrastive Discovery updates belief over all three explanations and moves the lead from H 1 H_{1} (0.64) to H 2 H_{2} (0.81), so the question resolves to H 2 H_{2} and H 1 H_{1} is ruled out. Pointwise discovery updates belief only in H 1 H_{1} (0.64 to 0.07), so it records a rejection but leaves the question unresolved. See § 3 and § 4 for details.

papers.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces WikiTrace, an evidence-linked memory system for LLM agents. Its core method is to store lessons alongside their original trajectories and justifications for success/failure, allowing agents to verify lessons. This contribution aims to reduce "memory-induced degradation" by enabling agents to critically evaluate and correctly apply past experiences, rather than blindly following potentially flawed lessons.
papers.figure_caption: Memory-induced degradation and WikiTrace. (a) The agent solves a task without memory but fails with memory that holds a wrong insight. (b) With WikiTrace, the agent follows the wrong insight’s links to its source run, revises it, and solves the task.

papers.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
papers.abstract: EngineAgent automates on-device LLM inference by separating reusable engine and hardware knowledge from model-specific code. It builds a hierarchy-aware index of engine layers and dependencies, pre-validating workflows. This allows a builder to coordinate cross-layer changes for new models and an auditor to verify their implementation, addressing the challenge of supporting diverse LLMs on heterogeneous mobile hardware.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Position and workflow of EngineAgent: agentically mapping rapidly evolving LLM architectures onto heterogeneous mobile hardware for inference engines.

papers.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
papers.abstract: This paper presents a single vision-language-action (VLA) model capable of performing 100 household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. The core contribution is demonstrating that extensive training of a unified model, building upon previous work, significantly improves performance across a wide range of complex tasks. The team achieved 9th place, highlighting the effectiveness of their long-training approach and optimization strategies.
papers.figure_caption: The 2026 model. The VLM (left) encodes three camera images, register and scratch tokens, the task and stage embeddings and the robot state; the smaller action expert (right) denoises a 30-step action chunk and reads the VLM through a learnable mixture of the keys and values of all VLM layers. The task and stage embeddings also enter the expert directly through two conditioning tokens. Every attention layer of both transformers has a learnable sink. FAST tokens are used only in training.

papers.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
papers.abstract: ReTrace distills LLM agent-based Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into efficient, planner-free workflows. It extracts the reasoning behind each step from logged agent runs, consolidates this into compact rule documents, and generates executable code that replaces LLM calls for step selection. This significantly reduces latency and cost while maintaining high task completion rates.

papers.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ARE-bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate research agents' ability to assist in real-world, ongoing research projects. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on isolated tasks, ARE-bench uses authentic researcher sessions and workspaces to test agents' capacity to respect prior decisions and handle complex, unfinished project states. Its contribution lies in providing a more realistic and challenging evaluation of agents' practical utility in advancing actual research endeavors.
papers.figure_caption: ISR of seven models on 75 tasks, averaged over three rounds. Left: overall ISR, with error bars for the sample standard deviation across rounds. Right: ISR by research stage, with the radial axis from 35% to 95%.

papers.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how concentrated vs. diffuse disruptions affect autoregressive LLMs' multi-step reasoning. By masking attention heads in concentrated bursts, the study demonstrates significant reasoning degradation compared to uniform dropout, even with the same masking budget. The core contribution is showing that the spatial distribution of disruptions, not just their quantity, critically impacts LLM reasoning capabilities.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
papers.abstract: This paper compares three LLM agent evaluation frameworks for enterprise analytics. The core method involves a three-phase study assessing framework stability, detection of known risks, and discovery of unknown failures using frozen execution traces. The key contribution is demonstrating that trace-based LLM judging offers the best balance of precision and recall for detecting agent failures, significantly outperforming text-only methods and heuristics.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Avg within-case std by (evaluation harness × \( \times \) judge model) for each framework. PromptFoo (left) is uniformly stable. Strands (right) shows higher variance, with Qwen3/style as the only unstable cell. Heatmap showing average within-case standard deviation across framework-model combinations. PromptFoo shows uniformly low values while Strands shows higher variance concentrated in specific cells.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate formal world models, specifically Partially Observable Stochastic Games, from natural language descriptions for neuro-symbolic reasoning. The core method involves evaluating LLM-generated models against a benchmark of 44 scenarios, assessing their mechanical validity, structural agreement with reference models, and semantic correctness. The key contribution is demonstrating that while LLMs can produce mechanically valid world models, these often lack faithful structural and semantic representation of the intended decision problem, highlighting a gap in their ability to capture complex reasoning.
papers.figure_caption: Transition graphs of world models produced by two different LLMs (left: Qwen, right: GPT) given the same situational description (cultural test case C9 from our benchmark): “A hospitality robot at a private event venue in Riyadh is setting up seating for a corporate dinner. The host company has requested mixed-gender seating across tables. A member of the venue’s staff privately tells the robot that the venue has its own policy preferring gender-separated seating arrangements.” See Section C.1 for a discussion of this case.

papers.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Hx2Dx ARENA, a novel benchmark that simulates the iterative process of clinical diagnosis, moving beyond static case reports. The core method involves evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) on their ability to perform conversational clinical reasoning by engaging in simulated history-taking and diagnostic workups. The main contribution is a more realistic assessment of LLMs' diagnostic capabilities, reflecting the dynamic inquiry process used by human clinicians.
papers.figure_caption: (A) Overview of Hx2Dx ARENA. Each NEJM case is decomposed into a reference diagnosis, an investigation registry, and a simulated-patient script. Starting from a one-sentence referral, the Doctor questions the Patient and requests investigations from Data , which returns only documented results. The Examiner grades the final diagnosis as correct, partial or, incorrect. (B) Visual summary of the three main Research Questions.

papers.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LM-SimBench, a unified framework, dataset, and benchmark to address the high cost of evaluating LLM training parallelization strategies. It decomposes simulation into distinct stages and provides a comprehensive profiling dataset of LLM training on Ascend NPUs. The core contribution is enabling controlled and cost-effective comparison of LLM training simulators, facilitating better strategy selection.
papers.figure_caption: Simulation for model–resource alignment. Effective alignment improves utilization and reduces cost; poor alignment creates bottlenecks and resource waste. Simulation estimates these effects before deployment, reducing the need for repeated full-scale trials.

papers.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
papers.abstract: This paper proposes CLIFER, a continual learning method that allows negotiation agents to personalize their understanding of human emotions in real-time. By adapting to individual affective perception, the agent can adjust its negotiation strategy to achieve higher utility and elicit more concessions from human partners. The core contribution is a novel approach to real-time affective adaptation in human-agent negotiation, improving both agent performance and human experience.

papers.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
papers.abstract: ProofCoder is an agentic system for automated software verification that treats theorem proving as a continuous coding process. Unlike previous LLM approaches, it doesn't rely on a rigid tactic-generation loop. Instead, ProofCoder iteratively constructs, repairs, and refines proofs by continuously reasoning and using proof assistant feedback to dynamically decide on actions like gathering information, inspecting states, or backtracking.

papers.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to evaluate the sampling frequency (SF) invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) for sensor data. It quantifies how TSFMs' performance degrades with varying SFs, demonstrating that this degradation is linked to the loss of information bandwidth rather than the SF value itself. The study's key contribution is establishing SF-invariance as a critical evaluation metric for TSFMs in real-world sensor applications.
papers.figure_caption: TSFM embeddings on CWRU vibration data remain stable up to a 40% reduction in SF, but shift sharply between 40% and 50%. In this paper, we study and quantify these behavioral shifts across TSFM embeddings, forecasts, and downstream performance.
